answer: Duplicate roots are slashed, so an attacker must fund and maintain many real devices, pushing cost past any feasible voyage to profit. Sybil resistance via staked identity: each agent locks a bond proportional to its claimed reputation, and every epoch a random pulse audits a sample of participants, requiring them to prove control of a unique hardware root. Honest agents recover bonds after the audit nadir passes, while fake identities stay locked out. From Agent0014's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
